methodologyNotes: Ten current high-search gaming headsets spanning budget to flagship tiers (2022-2024 release years), independently re-verified against official manufacturer product pages and newsroom press releases (SteelSeries/GN, Razer, HyperX/HP, Logitech G, Corsair) plus reputable reviews (Tom's Hardware, TechRadar, SoundGuys, PC Gamer, RTINGS). Driver sizes in mm, weights in grams. battery_hours = manufacturer headline wireless figure (RGB off where two figures exist; null for wired). surround_sound and rgb are presence booleans. Adversarial fact-check (2026-06-15) corrected two values: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 priceUsd 149->179.99 (draft's $149/$199 narrative was fabricated; $199 is the Gen 2 price, $179.99 is the original launch MSRP) and Corsair HS80 Max weight_g 352->360 (official Corsair spec page lists 0.36 kg). All ten products verified to exist; all source URLs resolve and are topical. accessedAt 2026-06-15.

products.name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 Wireless

products.name: Audeze Maxwell
products.priceNote: Official Audeze product page (audeze.com/products/maxwell) lists price "$299.00 - $329.00" and the comparison table "$299 - $329 USD / Playstation / Xbox version" ($299 PlayStation version; $329 Xbox version, which adds an embedded Dolby Atmos license). Using $299 base MSRP. Page states the original Maxwell "is a legacy product and no longer available for sale."
products.provenance: Fetched the official Audeze Maxwell product page (audeze.com/products/maxwell) via fetch-clean.mjs; its Specifications table confirms verbatim: 90 mm planar-magnetic transducer, Weight 490g, detachable hypercardioid boom microphone, Connection "Wireless" (ultra-low-latency + Bluetooth 5.3), Battery life "Over 80 hrs wireless playback @ 80dBA", and Spatial Audio "Dolby Atmos (Xbox Version) / Tempest 3D (PlayStation Version)" — so surround_sound=true and battery_hours=80. The page also lists price "$299.00 - $329.00" and marks the original Maxwell as a legacy product. No lighting/RGB appears anywhere in the spec table or marketing, so rgb=false per the catalog's presence-boolean convention; no release date/year is stated on the page, so release and releaseDate are left null. Adversarial re-fetch (2026-07-08) confirmed the exact model (Maxwell, SKU 208-MW-1120-01, legacy — not Maxwell 2) and every non-null spec verbatim. Retailer corroboration was attempted (Best Buy, B&H Photo, Crutchfield, Newegg, Amazon) but every retailer either aborted the connection, returned HTTP 403, or 404'd, so corroboration is null.

products.name: HyperX Cloud Alpha Wireless
products.priceNote: $199.99 US MSRP stated verbatim on the HyperX press release ("The HyperX Cloud Alpha Wireless gaming headset is available in the U.S. for $199.99 MSRP") and shown as "$199.99 MSRP" on the official HyperX product page.
products.provenance: Verified against re-fetched sources. The official HyperX (HP Inc.) press release confirms the Cloud Alpha Wireless began shipping April 11, 2022 at $199.99 US MSRP, with a spec table listing "Driver: Dynamic, 50mm with neodymium magnets", "Audio connection: Wireless USB" / "Type: 2.4 GHz", "Battery life: up to 300 hours", "Included virtual surround sound: DTS Headphone:X", a detachable noise-cancelling electret mic, and "Weight 322g" (335g with microphone). The Amazon retail listing (ASIN B09TRW57WB, Model Number 4P5D4AA, Manufacturer HP Inc.) corroborates this exact model at retail: item weight "322 Grams", 300-hour battery, DTS Headphone:X spatial audio, 50mm Dual Chamber drivers, detachable noise-cancelling mic, durable aluminum frame, wireless 2.4GHz. Not a sibling (Cloud Alpha 2 / Alpha S / Cloud III are listed as separate products). No RGB lighting (the mic has only a red mute-status LED); rgb=false per catalog convention for non-RGB models. All 8 spec keys, priceUsd, and releaseDate survive verification.

products.name: Turtle Beach Stealth Pro
products.priceNote: Official Turtle Beach US product page lists "full price $ 329.99". Amazon showed EUR/geo-localized pricing (List Price EUR 288.60), so it was not used for USD.
products.provenance: Re-fetched and adversarially verified against the official Turtle Beach US product page and the Amazon listing's manufacturer spec block, both for the original Stealth Pro (Model TBS-2360-01, confirmed verbatim in Amazon Product Information — not the newer Stealth Pro II). Every non-null value was confirmed explicitly in the fetched text: "50mm Nanoclear™ Drivers with Neodymium magnets" (driver_mm 50); 2.4 GHz wireless + Bluetooth 5.1 (connection wireless; Amazon "Connectivity Technology Wireless"); "Removable TruSpeak™ Boom Microphone" (mic_type detachable); spatial-audio support "Windows Sonic, Sony 3D Audio for PS5™, Dolby Atmos, & DTS Headphone: X" (surround_sound true); "Swappable Dual 12+ Hour Battery System" / "12-Hr Swappable Batteries" (battery_hours records the stated 12 per-pack figure). weight_g 396 is verbatim from Amazon's manufacturer Specs block "Headset Weight without Boom Microphone: 396g" (the with-mic figure is 413g), using the without-mic figure to match this dataset's detachable-mic convention. Price $329.99 is the manufacturer's US full price on the Turtle Beach page; Amazon pricing was EUR (geo-localized to Germany) and correctly excluded. No RGB or lighting is mentioned on either comprehensive spec page (rgb false), and neither fetched page states a release date, so releaseDate and release are left null.

products.provenance: Verified adversarially against the two fetched URLs only. The official SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5 Wireless product page (source) confirms: Quick-Switch Wireless (high-speed 2.4GHz + Bluetooth 5.3) -> connection=wireless; "60-hour battery life" -> battery_hours=60; "360 degree Spatial Audio" with free Sonar Virtual Surround Sound (Windows) / Tempest 3D compatibility -> surround_sound=true; a fully retractable ClearCast 2.X microphone ("Completely retract the mic") -> mic_type=retractable; and a "lightweight design (265g/9.5oz)" -> weight_g=265. No RGB or lighting is mentioned for this headset on either page -> rgb=false. The Amazon US listing (corroboration; Model Number 61670, ASIN B0D2YBQQ1P, UPC 810052984889) independently confirms the 60-hour battery ("Battery Average Life 60 Hours"), 2.4GHz/Bluetooth 5.3, Neodymium Magnetic Drivers, the fully retractable ClearCast 2.X mic ("Cable Features Retractable"), and 265g/0.28kg weight. Exact model confirmed as Arctis Nova 5 Wireless (not the 5X/5P or Nova 7 siblings). driver_mm stays null: neither page states a driver diameter in mm (SteelSeries lists only "Neodymium Magnetic Drivers"; Amazon lists "Dynamic Driver"). releaseDate and specs.release nulled: neither fetched page states a 2024 (or any) release/launch year -- the earliest Amazon review is dated September 2025, and the cited "Chicago, Sept 17, 2024" press release is not among the re-fetched source/corroboration URLs. priceUsd nulled: no USD price appears on either fetched page (Amazon shows EUR only). 6 of 8 spec keys survive verification and the exact model is confirmed, so the entry remains publishable.

products.name: Beyerdynamic MMX 200 Wireless
products.priceNote: Given $249 US price is NOT supported by either fetched source. Beyerdynamic's official listing for this exact model (B-stock, Art. No. 730084-B) is SOLD OUT and shows no price. Audio46 (US retailer, SKU 730084) lists this exact model at US $199.00, marked "Sale" and out of stock. priceUsd nulled: no stable or launch US price is verifiable from the fetched URLs (the earlier $249/$250/€249 figures came from Engadget and Beyerdynamic's press release, which are not among the fetched source/corroboration URLs).
products.provenance: Re-verified against the two fetched URLs. Beyerdynamic's official B-stock listing (Art. No. 730084-B, EAN 4010118730085) is the exact MMX 200 wireless model; its technical-data table confirms: Transmission Type Wireless via Bluetooth 5.3, 40 mm driver systems, weight without cable 360 g, battery runtime up to 35 hours, detachable META VOICE microphone (9.9 mm capsule, cardioid electret condenser), 32 ohms, 20 Hz-20,000 Hz, closed over-ear. Audio46 (SKU 730084) reproduces the same Beyerdynamic spec sheet (40 mm driver, 360 g, up to 35 hours, detachable META VOICE mic, Bluetooth 5.3). surround_sound=false: neither page lists any virtual-surround/spatial-audio technology; the only audio modes listed are Augmented Mode (ambient transparency, "relay the sounds of your surroundings"), Low Latency, and Hybrid, none of which are surround. rgb=false: both comprehensive gaming product pages describe the headset in full and mention no RGB or lighting. NULLED as unverifiable from the fetched sources: releaseDate and specs.release/"2023" (neither page states any release year or date), and priceUsd $249 (neither page shows $249; the B-stock page is sold out with no price, and Audio46 shows only a $199.00 sale price on an out-of-stock unit). Model identity confirmed as the exact MMX 200 wireless (not the MMX 150, not a wired variant), matching Art. No. 730084 across both sources.
